literal: Those of killing-occupation who are undiscerning people, vile-occupation-holders they are, in the mind of those who discern baseness.
translation: In the estimation of those who discern the baseness of slaughter, people whose occupation is killing are regarded as doers of the vilest deeds.
modern: கொலை செய்வதன் இழிவை உணர்ந்தவர்களின் மனதில், கொலையைத் தொழிலாகக் கொண்ட மனிதர்கள் இழிவான செயலைச் செய்பவர்களாகவே கருதப்படுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet explains how those who kill are perceived by wise and compassionate people. The word 'mākkaḷ' refers to humans who lack higher moral discernment and act on animal instincts. To those who truly understand the inherent baseness ('punmai') of taking a life, anyone engaged in the profession of killing ('kolaivinaiyar') is seen as performing the lowest, most degraded deeds ('pulaivinaiyar'). The verse emphasizes that true social and moral standing is determined by one's compassion, not by outward human form.
